questions.knowledge_point: Finding a Component of a Vector With Respect to a Given Orthogonal Basis
questions.problem:
Given the orthogonal basis $B$ of ${R}^{3}$ and the vector $x$ below, find the value of $29{x}_{1}$, where ${x}_{1}$ is the first component of $[x]_{B}.$

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4 \\ -2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ -3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-18 \\ 5 \\ -17\end{aligned}]},\,x=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${q}_{1},\,{q}_{2},\,{q}_{3}.$ 

Since $B$ is an orthogonal basis, we have that $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]$, where ${x}_{i}=\frac{x\cdot {q}_{i}}{{q}_{i}\cdot {q}_{i}}.$ Computing ${x}_{1},$ we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\frac{x\cdot {q}_{1}}{{q}_{1}\cdot {q}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{5\cdot 3+(-1)\cdot 4+2\cdot (-2)}{{3}^{2}+{4}^{2}+(-2)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{15-4-4}{9+16+4} \\  & =\frac{7}{29}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
29{x}_{1}=29\cdot \frac{7}{29}=7.
$$

questions.problem:
Given the orthogonal basis $B$ of ${R}^{2}$ and the vector $x$ below, find the value of $20{x}_{2},$ where ${x}_{2}$ is the second component of $[x]_{B}.$

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -8\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]},\,x=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${q}_{1},\,{q}_{2}.$ 

Since $B$ is an orthogonal basis, we have that $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$, where ${x}_{i}=\frac{x\cdot {q}_{i}}{{q}_{i}\cdot {q}_{i}}.$ Computing ${x}_{2},$ we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\frac{x\cdot {q}_{2}}{{q}_{2}\cdot {q}_{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-1)\cdot (-2)+1\cdot (-1)}{(-2)^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2-1}{4+1} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
20{x}_{2}=20\cdot \frac{1}{5}=4.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Components of a Vector With Respect to a Given Orthonormal Basis
questions.problem:
Given the **orthonormal** basis $B$ of ${R}^{3}$ and the vector $x$ below, find the value of $\frac{1}{2}{x}_{1}$, where ${x}_{1}$ is the first component of $[x]_{B}.$

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-\frac{2}{\sqrt{14}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{14}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{14}}\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{\sqrt{35}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{35}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{35}}\end{aligned}]},\,x=[\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{10} \\ \frac{\sqrt{10}}{2} \\ -\frac{\sqrt{10}}{2}\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${q}_{1},\,{q}_{2},\,{q}_{3}.$ 

Since $B$ is an orthonormal basis, we have that $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]$, where ${x}_{i}=x\cdot {q}_{i}.$ Computing ${x}_{1},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =x\cdot {q}_{1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{10} \\ \frac{\sqrt{10}}{2} \\ -\frac{\sqrt{10}}{2}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}-\frac{3}{2} \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\frac{1}{2}{x}_{1}=\frac{1}{2}\cdot (-2)=-1.
$$

questions.problem: Given the **orthonormal** basis $B={[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}]}$ of ${R}^{2},$ find $[x]_{B}$ if $x=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${q}_{1},\,{q}_{2}.$ 

Since $B$ is an orthonormal basis, we have that $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$, where ${x}_{i}=x\cdot {q}_{i}.$ Computing the components of $x,$ we get the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}]=\frac{4}{\sqrt{2}}-\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}} \\ {x}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}]=\frac{4}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{6}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have 

$$
[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{6}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

questions.problem:
Given the orthogonal basis $B$ of ${R}^{2}$ and the vector $x$ below, find the value of $6{x}_{1},$ where ${x}_{1}$ is the first component of $[x]_{B}.$

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 12\end{aligned}]},\,x=[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ 8\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${q}_{1},\,{q}_{2}.$ 

Since $B$ is an orthogonal basis, we have that $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$, where ${x}_{i}=\frac{x\cdot {q}_{i}}{{q}_{i}\cdot {q}_{i}}.$ Computing ${x}_{1},$ we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\frac{x\cdot {q}_{1}}{{q}_{1}\cdot {q}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{(-9)\cdot 4+8\cdot 2}{{4}^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-36+16}{16+4} \\  & =\frac{-20}{20} \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
6{x}_{1}=6\cdot (-1)=-6.
$$
